title: Book: The Psychology of Money — Morgan Housel (2020)
publisher: Artha Kavach original summary of a book's ideas (paraphrase, not a quotation; the author's opinion, not settled fact) — pending manual verification
text: Morgan Housel argues that how you behave with money matters more than how much you know about it. His central ideas: wealth is the money you did not spend, so it is invisible; staying wealthy needs a margin of safety and room for error, because survival lets compounding work for decades; define 'enough' so you stop risking what you have for what you do not need; a few big wins usually drive most of the results (tails drive everything), so patience beats frequent tinkering; luck and risk shape outcomes, so be humble about both success and failure; and the highest return on money is control over your own time. Practical takeaways: save even without a specific goal, avoid comparing yourself with people whose goals differ, and plan to be wrong sometimes. Caution: it is a book of stories and principles, not a step-by-step plan, and some anecdotes are US-based.
